request_payload.title: Gain of function SCN1A disease-causing variants: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum and functional studies guiding the choice of effective antiseizure medication.

mentions.sentence: In our cohort, >50% of patients manifested focal epilepsies, which are thus a frequent feature of SCN1A pathogenic variants beyond DS and GEFS+.

candidates.label: EEG with series of focal spikes

mentions.sentence: Functional studies of three representative variants showed a gain of channel function.

candidates.summary: The variant protein is overactive: in these disorders that usually means synaptic vesicles fuse too readily, or neurotransmitter is released when it should not

mentions.sentence: Sodium channel blockers never worsened seizures, and 50% of patients experienced long periods of seizure freedom.

candidates.label: Quinidine (KCNT1 channel blocker, repurposed)
candidates.summary: An antiarrhythmic drug and partial KCNT1 antagonist tried in KCNT1 gain-of-function epilepsies, with mixed results.

candidates.label: Sodium channel blocking anti-seizure medicines (class)
candidates.summary: A class of established anti-seizure medicines that reduce sodium channel activity. Published responses differ by gene and by variant mechanism.

candidates.label: 4-Phenylbutyrate / glycerol phenylbutyrate (chemical chaperone)
candidates.summary: An FDA-approved drug (for urea-cycle disorders) that acts as a chemical chaperone, helping unstable or misfolded proteins fold and reach their working location.

candidates.label: Kv7 potassium channel openers (ezogabine / retigabine, XEN496)
candidates.summary: Drugs that open KCNQ2/KCNQ3 (Kv7) potassium channels, studied in KCNQ2 encephalopathy due to loss-of-function variants.

candidates.label: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (early, for Krabbe disease)
candidates.summary: Donor blood stem cells that supply galactocerebrosidase. The only disease-modifying option for Krabbe disease, and only effective when done very early.
